comparison: Both address the three-phase model of Q-nMT assembly (C20, C32-C45). OpenEval finds the evidence SUPPORTED with converging data from multiple approaches. Peer review rates it UNCERTAIN, with Reviewer 1 concerned that the evidence relies too heavily on nocodazole sensitivity as the primary methodology, questioning whether this single approach sufficiently establishes distinct phases.

Both evaluate Aurora B/Ipl1 and CPC component requirements (C21, C68-C72, C79). OpenEval finds the claims SUPPORTED by multiple independent approaches with appropriate controls. Peer review rates UNCERTAIN, with Reviewer 1 noting that phenotypic differences are 'really subtle' for many mutants (bir1, slk19), questioning whether the magnitude of effects supports the claimed critical roles.

Both address Kar3/Cik1 involvement in phase I (C22, C95-C98). OpenEval finds SUPPORTED by localization and deletion mutant data. Peer review rates the broader kinesin findings (including Kar3/Cik1, Cin8, Kip1) as SUPPORTED, with the editor noting 'experimental support is overall solid' and Reviewer 3 identifying kinesin involvement as a strength.

Both evaluate Cin8's role in phase II bundle thickening (C25, C99-C101). OpenEval finds SUPPORTED by quantitative measurements and nocodazole assays. Peer review includes this in broader SUPPORTED assessment of kinesin findings, with no specific challenges to Cin8 data.

Both address Kip1's role in phase III stabilization (C26, C102-C105). OpenEval finds SUPPORTED by localization and nocodazole sensitivity data. Peer review includes this in SUPPORTED assessment of sequential kinesin requirements, noting solid experimental foundation.

Both evaluate kinetochore-MT attachment requirements using ndc80-1 (C4, C27, C66-C67, C79). OpenEval finds SUPPORTED with appropriate temperature controls. Peer review rates UNCERTAIN, expressing concern about meiosis-specific factors like Mam1 being present in proliferating cells and noting subtle phenotypic differences for some mutants.

Both address kinetochore clustering and inter-kinetochore interactions (C4, C27, C80-C89). OpenEval finds SUPPORTED by extensive phenotypic analysis of deletion mutants and genetic interactions. Peer review rates UNCERTAIN, with Reviewer 1 noting subtle phenotypic differences and puzzlement about meiosis-specific factors, questioning the strength of evidence for critical roles.

Both evaluate Bim1 genetic interactions and functional redundancy (C73-C77). OpenEval finds SUPPORTED by genetic interaction experiments showing synthetic phenotypes. Peer review also rates SUPPORTED, noting the strong bim1Δ bir1Δ double mutant phenotype supports redundancy interpretation despite subtle single mutant effects.

Both address kinetochore-MT independence for bundle maintenance (C90-C94). OpenEval finds SUPPORTED by laser ablation and conditional inactivation experiments. Peer review also rates SUPPORTED, with no specific challenges to these maintenance findings; included in 'overall solid' experimental support.

Both evaluate Tub3 tubulin isotype involvement in phase II (C54-C65). OpenEval finds SUPPORTED by imaging, phenotypic analysis, and western blots. Peer review also rates SUPPORTED, with no specific critiques of tubulin data; appears part of solid experimental foundation noted by editor.

Both address Kip3/She1-mediated disassembly mechanisms (C5, C28-C30, C108-C119). OpenEval finds SUPPORTED by multiple lines of evidence including cycloheximide treatment and mutant analysis. Peer review also rates SUPPORTED, with Reviewer 3 explicitly identifying kinesin involvement in disassembly as a strength and editor noting important insights.

Both evaluate claims about Q-nMT disassembly timing and cell cycle re-entry (C6, C31, C120-C125). OpenEval finds SUPPORTED by time-lapse imaging and quantification. Peer review rates UNSUPPORTED, with Reviewer 3 explicitly stating 'the claim that the Q-nMT functions as a checkpoint effector that inhibits re-entry into the cell cycle' is not supported, suggesting correlation but not causation.

Both address time-restricted assembly signals and viability (C49-C53). OpenEval finds SUPPORTED by nocodazole pulse-chase and viability assays. Peer review splits assessment: C46-C51 (physicochemical properties) rated SUPPORTED, but C52-C53 (viability links) addressed separately in R3 as UNSUPPORTED.

Both evaluate viability and fitness consequences of Q-nMT defects (C52-C53, plus C18-C19, C78). OpenEval finds SUPPORTED by viability assays establishing physiological importance. Peer review rates UNSUPPORTED, with Reviewer 1 explicitly stating 'evidence shown are insufficient to provide a direct link between defects in cell viability and aberrant Q-nMT formation.'

Both address whether bundle stability can be explained by physicochemical properties (C46-C48). OpenEval finds SUPPORTED by experiments showing coexistence of dynamic/stable MTs and pH manipulation. Peer review also rates SUPPORTED, with Reviewer 3 explicitly acknowledging this as a strength and editor noting it as an important insight.

Both reference Q-nMT structure, function, and physiological importance (C1, C11-C19). OpenEval finds SUPPORTED based on prior work and current viability data. Peer review partially overlaps (C18-C19, C78) in R3 rated UNSUPPORTED, challenging the direct link between Q-nMT defects and viability.

OpenEval finds Q-nMT bundle generality across cell types and quiescence conditions (C40-C41) SUPPORTED by imaging data. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these specific claims about generality.

Both address kinesin length regulation and phase-specific summary (C106-C107). OpenEval finds SUPPORTED by phenotypic analysis of kip3Δ and kip2Δ mutants. Peer review includes C107 in broader SUPPORTED assessment of kinesin findings with solid experimental support.

Both address chronological aging viability (C78, C87). OpenEval finds SUPPORTED by viability assays showing reduced survival. Peer review rates UNSUPPORTED as part of broader challenge to linking Q-nMT defects directly to viability outcomes.

OpenEval finds background claims about microtubule structure and dynamics (C7-C10) SUPPORTED as established knowledge. No corresponding peer review evaluation found; these are introductory context claims.

Both address speculative hypotheses in Discussion (C126-C133). OpenEval rates UNCERTAIN, noting these are proposals for future investigation rather than established results. Peer review rates SUPPORTED in the sense that speculative claims are appropriately framed after revision, with Reviewer 3 satisfied with precise language.
